decisions.executionNote: Begin elevated, gradual elbow-up approaches to red nut on left and yellow nut on right; keep grippers open.
Finish downward wrist orientation above the two same-side nuts, retaining elbow-up continuity and height clearance.
Descend toward nut grasp height with small wrist-image centering corrections; table-height estimate remains uncertain.
Fine-center, close on red and yellow nuts at grasp height, then make a short retention-check lift.
Both nuts appear retained. Lift clear and carry each over its same-color bolt in its own workspace; refine insertion alignment from wrist views.
Center red nut slightly right/forward from wrist view and lower both nuts slowly toward bolt engagement; keep closed.
Refine lateral alignment from visible bolt caps, then begin a slow clockwise threading turn with a small axial descent.
Caps still appear laterally offset through both holes. Make a small camera-aligned correction and continue gentle clockwise insertion.
Pause rotation and correct the remaining cap offset along wrist-image right, with only a shallow axial adjustment.
Yellow cap appears centered; finish this clockwise stroke on both nuts with shallow thread-following descent and a small remaining red correction.
Open to let the nuts settle and reset wrist yaw without backing the nuts off; inspect red alignment before the next stroke.
Red nut fell beside its bolt; approach its new position open. Regrasp the seated yellow nut and apply another short clockwise threading stroke.
Corrected rejected tensor; same intended centering, red regrasp and check lift, with open-gripper yellow yaw reset. No compensation for rejected motion.
Carry retained red nut back over its bolt using head-camera alignment and approach gently. Regrasp yellow and apply another clockwise stroke with shallow descent.
Red nut has visibly tipped; release and lift clear to reassess rather than force insertion. Reset the open yellow wrist for another tightening stroke.
Approach upright red nut again with corrected vertical wrist orientation. Continue yellow clockwise tightening, following the thread by only a few millimeters.
Fine-center and lift the red nut well above the bolt before translating. Release yellow and reset its wrist without reversing the nut.
Re-estimate red bolt alignment using the lower tabletop/object heights indicated by pickup RGB; translate while high, then approach. Continue a shallow yellow tightening stroke.
Apply only a small lateral red correction and lower gently to engage the bolt, then begin threading. Release and lift clear of yellow to inspect the seated pair.
Yellow remains seated after release. Make a small isolated red translation to resolve the remaining cap offset; reset the right wrist while clear.
The isolated translation moved the red cap toward the hole; continue a smaller correction without lowering. Move the open right arm to an elevated central staging position.
Red cap now appears centered through the nut. Apply a controlled clockwise stroke with shallow thread-following descent; keep the right arm clear and open.
Red showed contact deflection during turning. Release and withdraw before more forceful motion; inspect whether the nut stays seated, resetting yaw while clear.
Red nut is separate again. Approach its observed resting position with the wrist corrected to vertical, keeping the right arm out of the left workspace.
Fine-center the red nut, close and lift it clear. Return its wrist yaw to an easier visual-alignment heading while retaining the nut.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating for unexecuted motion. Translate red at clearance with fixed orientation to isolate planar alignment.
Hold wrist yaw fixed and lower the red nut with a tiny lateral correction, checking cap motion before committing to threading.
Continue a slow axial red approach with no rotation or lateral motion, checking whether the bolt enters the nut without tipping.
Red nut tipped on contact; release and withdraw instead of forcing it. Move the left arm clear toward the untouched purple nut for a staged transfer.
Approach purple nut with left wrist-image centering. Move the right arm back within its workspace to keep the central staging area clear.
Fine-center purple in the left gripper, descend to pickup height, close, and make a short retention-check lift before staging.
Purple was not retained. Reopen and correct the wrist-image vertical direction using the observed motion, approaching slowly without closing until centered.
Use the now-observed vertical image response to finish centering purple, close on it, and lift for a visual retention check.
Purple is visibly retained. Carry it at clearance to the middle for a table-assisted transfer, keeping the right arm back and the arms uncrossed.
Lower purple onto the middle of the table and release for a staged transfer. Keep the right arm stationary until the left withdraws.
Withdraw the open left hand upward and into its workspace. Only after clearance, begin the right-hand approach to the staged purple nut.
Red now appears seated on its bolt; approach it open for tightening rather than lifting it again. Bring the right hand above the staged purple nut, keeping arms separated.
Lower and regrasp the seated red nut without lifting it. Descend the right gripper toward the central purple nut with small wrist-image centering corrections.
Recenter the left fingers on the red nut rather than its stem, then regrasp for a short test turn. Center purple, close, and lift to verify the staged pickup.
Red remains centered and seated; continue a slow clockwise tightening stroke. Lift retained purple clear and carry it above its matching right-side bolt.
Reset the open left wrist without reversing red. Lower purple slowly with a small lateral correction, holding its fore-aft position to isolate insertion alignment.
Continue a shallow red tightening stroke. Correct purple fore-aft alignment at constant height, using the observed wrist-image direction before further descent.
Purple cap now appears within the hole after fore-aft correction; start a gentle clockwise threading stroke. Release and lift away from red to inspect its seated state.
Purple shifted during contact; release and withdraw to let it settle and inspect before another stroke. Red remains seated after release; reset its wrist while clear.
Purple is separate from its bolt; approach its new resting position with the right gripper open. Begin returning the clear left arm toward origin with gradual configuration-continuous motion.
Regrasp the centered purple nut and lift it clear before translating toward the bolt. Complete the left arm's gradual return toward origin with its gripper open.
Purple slipped rather than lifting. Reopen and approach its newly observed resting position; pause at pickup height for a fresh centering check.
Purple is below the finger center in the wrist image; correct fore-aft alignment before closing, then make a short lift to verify retention.
Purple is visibly retained. Lift clear, then translate above its bolt at fixed wrist heading; keep the returned left arm still and open.
Lower purple axially at fixed yaw and planar position, checking engagement before applying any tightening rotation.
Purple cap is entering the hole but remains slightly offset. Make a millimeter-scale centering correction and shallow descent before turning.
Finish a submillimeter purple centering correction, then test a slow clockwise threading stroke with only 1 mm of axial descent.
Purple did not stay centered during the test turn. Stop rotation, translate gently toward the visible cap, and release to let it seat without forced insertion.
Purple is tipped after release. Withdraw the open gripper and allow it to settle; reset the wrist to a vertical approach while clear of the pair.
Purple remains supported on the bolt after settling. Reapproach open and vertically, with a small centering correction, to inspect its seating before regrasping.
Center the right fingers around the supported purple nut, regrasp without lifting, and test only a small clockwise turn at constant height.
The purple nut remains supported after the small test turn. Continue a controlled clockwise stroke with only 2 mm of thread-following descent, keeping the left arm open at origin.
Purple now appears fully seated with its cap flush. Open and lift clear while resetting right wrist yaw; make a small left-origin correction.
Purple stays seated after release. Begin the right arm's gradual return toward origin while both grippers remain open and all pairs stay undisturbed.
Complete the right arm's gradual return to origin, keeping both grippers open. The three pairs appear seated; await the environment's completion signal.
Yellow still shows more exposed internal thread than the other pairs. Reapproach it with the right arm for additional tightening; leave red and purple undisturbed.
The changed view shows yellow's cap seated flush without further contact. Avoid disturbing it and return the right arm to origin, keeping both grippers open.
The home view still shows substantial exposed yellow thread; reapproach to center the fingers on the nut itself and tighten further rather than infer completion from an oblique view.
Inspect yellow from a higher, vertical wrist view without contacting it, to distinguish true seating depth from the oblique appearance.
Yellow still shows exposed thread from the vertical view. Approach the seated nut axially with the gripper open, checking centering before further tightening.
Center the right fingers around yellow's seated nut, close without lifting, and test a small clockwise turn before a longer tightening stroke.
Yellow remains centered after the test turn. Continue clockwise tightening with a shallow 4 mm descent, preserving the seated red and purple pairs.
Release yellow and reset the wrist without backing off the nut. Its body appears offset from the finger center, so reassess centering before another grasp.
Recenter the right fingers on the yellow nut body, slightly above the previous grasp, then test a short clockwise turn without axial motion.
The yellow nut body is now centered in the fingers. Continue a clockwise threading stroke with 4 mm of gentle axial descent; keep the other pairs undisturbed.
Open the right fingers and reset wrist yaw without reversing the yellow nut, preparing another tightening stroke while preserving its seated alignment.
Regrasp the centered yellow nut and apply another clockwise tightening stroke with a shallow 3 mm axial descent. Keep red and purple undisturbed.
Yellow's depth changed little. Open and reset yaw while raising slightly to put the fingers on the nut body rather than below it; reassess before another turn.
Center the elevated fingers on yellow's nut body using the wrist view, then test a clockwise turn at constant height instead of pushing downward.
Yellow is centered in the fingers and still shows exposed internal thread. Continue a slow clockwise stroke with 4 mm of shallow axial descent, staying within wrist range.
Release yellow and lift the fingers fully clear before resetting yaw, avoiding possible contact that could undo tightening during the return stroke.
